unknowns.question: Where does install.sh live and how is it fetched (repo root rather than src/, URL pinned to a release tag) so it never ships into installs itself?
Where and in what form does an install record its Ang version (tag, commit SHA), and how does an upgrade baseline an instance with no record, such as ohnvm?
How would the workflow-improvement workflow keep a local version and changelog of improvements that an upgrading agent can reason over?
How would an upgrade skill merge upstream changes around local improvements: what makes a merge simple versus too much (the escape hatch), and what does taking only chosen parts look like?
What must each upstream release publish (tags, changelog) for an upgrading agent to know what changed?

knowns.fact: Requirements and options as Zac framed them

Gitignored *.local.* files (pilot.local.md, local styles) sit physically under src/.claude/ in this repo through the symlinks. Git never ships them, but any install route that copies src/ from disk would. Keeping them out of a release is this item's job

Copy-in fits, plugin doesn't: plugins can't ship rules or permissions, wipe user edits on update and namespace skills; candidates are plain degit/giget copy-in, copy-in plus a hash-manifest update, or copier
knowns.answers: Install route: plugin marketplace, copy script or degit-style clone, given users must own and edit their copy?

knowns.fact: Copying src/ brings project-context/README.md along with .claude/, so an install gets the conventions doc without library init copying it
knowns.answers: How does project-context/README.md reach a user's install, and should library init copy it?

knowns.fact: Zac's upgrade ambition: a recorded installed version, an upgrade skill that merges upstream around local improvements, a local changelog of workflow improvements, an escape hatch for oversized upgrades with pick-the-parts options, and a fast path for simple merges. Motivating case: ohnvm's pre-open-source Ang

decisions.decision: Install by copy-in of src/ (giget/degit --force) wrapped in a shipped install.sh, so the install is one copy-pasteable line. The script protects the user's .claude/settings.json and carries future install changes to every new user (Zac's call)

No uninstall command: removing a vanilla install is deleting skills, rules and project-context/, and local workflow improvements make automating it unreliable. Easy by hand, hard to automate (Zac's call)

The upgrade skill is in scope for this item and is to be built. Zac's deliberate exception to the intent's build-the-least: real value, and it belongs to the same logical unit of work as install, however big it has grown

install.sh merges an existing .claude/settings.json with node (already required, no jq dependency) and first keeps a backup of the user's original, in case the merge drops properties that mattered (Zac's call)
Tests ship with installs: a local workflow improvement may change shipped scripts, and having the tests on hand lets the user run them to check (Zac's call)
